project.name: Fleet Planner
project.purpose: Daily tool that fills in Driver and Vehicle columns of an uploaded Excel transport-request file, using a deterministic rules engine plus an optional AI review layer, then exports the same file with only those two columns changed.
project.status: actively developed, core pipeline working and validated against real user data

folder_structure.fleetplanner.db: SQLite database, created at runtime; a real snapshot has also been committed to the linked repo for AI testing purposes
folder_structure.app/db.py: all SQLite schema, migrations, and CRUD
folder_structure.app/rules_parser.py: free-text rule-line recognizer, used ONLY for AI-context notes, not hard rules
folder_structure.app/excel_import.py: daily request-file reader, produces Job objects
folder_structure.app/export.py: writes results into a copy of the original uploaded workbook
folder_structure.app/ui/main_window.py: QMainWindow, tab container, Settings PIN gating
folder_structure.app/ui/plan_day_tab.py: daily workflow screen, largest UI file
folder_structure.app/ui/drivers_tab.py: structured driver hard rules + AI notes
folder_structure.app/ui/vehicles_tab.py: vehicle roster, workshop/exclusion toggle, edit dialog
folder_structure.app/ui/settings_tab.py: API keys, PIN, digest refresh control
folder_structure.app/ui/entity_rules_widget.py: LEGACY, not imported by main_window.py as of last known state, superseded by drivers_tab.py/suppliers_tab.py

modules.responsibility: The deterministic core. No AI, no network calls, fully repeatable. Takes in-memory profiles + jobs, mutates jobs in place.
modules.does_not_import: app.db at module level -- db is passed as an explicit parameter to build_*_profiles functions, keeping this module testable standalone

dataclasses.name: DriverProfile
fields: shift_period ('morning' | 'evening' | None -- replaces shift_start, see HR-002 rework 2026-08-03)
max_working_hours_per_day (hard daily ceiling; None falls back to working_hours_per_day -- new 2026-08-03, replaces the removed MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY module constant)
busy_intervals (RUNTIME, list of (start, end, group_key) tuples -- group_key is the same_driver_key of the job that created that interval, or None)
dataclasses.critical_history_note: shift_start field was OMITTED from this dataclass during an earlier rewrite -- a real bug, fixed, then the field itself was replaced entirely by shift_period on 2026-08-03 (see HR-002 rework in CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 10). Any future field additions to drivers must be added here too, not just in the database.

dataclasses.name: VehicleProfile
fields: in_workshop (bool, merged from db.in_workshop OR db.excluded_from_planning)
busy_intervals (RUNTIME, list of (start, end, group_key) tuples)

dataclasses.name: SupplierHire
dataclasses.computed_property: label -- supplier_name if instance_number==1 else f'{supplier_name} {instance_number-1}'
dataclasses.note: RUNTIME ONLY, created dynamically during allocate(), never stored directly in the database -- only the resulting label text and supplier_id get persisted via finalized_jobs on Finalize

key_functions.name: build_driver_profiles
key_functions.purpose: reads drivers table, skips excluded_from_planning, computes month_overtime_so_far via db.get_driver_month_overtime_hours

key_functions.name: build_supplier_offerings
key_functions.purpose: reads supplier_offerings joined with suppliers, computes cumulative_hours_history via db.get_supplier_cumulative_hours

key_functions.name: _driver_qualifies_for_type
key_functions.purpose: exact-match check against license_types list; returns False entirely if license_types is empty (forces explicit configuration)

key_functions.name: _driver_is_off
key_functions.purpose: weekday check against off_days, with allow_override_days escape hatch

key_functions.name: _job_matches_shift_period
key_functions.purpose: hard rule (replaces _parse_shift_start_time/_job_is_before_shift_start, removed 2026-08-03): True if shift_period is None (no restriction), or if job.start_dt's time-of-day falls on the correct side of the noon cutoff for 'morning'/'evening'. See SHIFT_PERIOD_EVENING_CUTOFF_HOUR module constant.

key_functions.name: _overlaps_with_buffer
key_functions.purpose: checks time-interval overlap with a configurable minute buffer (default 0 as of 2026-08-03, was 30 -- see TB-001) for travel time between jobs -- now accepts an ignore_group_key parameter: intervals tagged with that same group_key are skipped, allowing overlap between rows the planner explicitly flagged as belonging to the same 'Same Driver' group.

key_functions.name: _type_matches
key_functions.purpose: case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized EXACT string comparison -- no fuzzy matching, deliberate design choice

key_functions.name: _vehicle_type_needs_vehicle
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, NEW-004 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: False for 'Driver Only' (case-insensitive) -- these rows need a qualified driver but no physical vehicle at all. Confirmed by a real PLANNED.xlsx row. Used across the main pass, gap-filler, and minimum-hours repair pass to skip vehicle-matching entirely for this type; assigned_vehicle_id/plate are left None/blank.

key_functions.name: _merged_hours
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, hour-accounting fix, HR-002 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: Returns the TRUE UNION of hours covered by the given (start, end, ...) intervals -- overlapping or touching intervals count once, not once each. Replaces naive summing everywhere occupied_seconds is read or written (main loop, gap-filler, minimum-hours repair pass) after a real PLANNED.xlsx showed a driver with ~17h 'occupied' (summed) against ~11h true (merged) work, which falsely tripped the daily ceiling. occupied_seconds is now always recomputed via this function immediately after busy_intervals changes, rather than incremented/decremented directly.

key_functions.name: allocate
key_functions.signature: allocate(jobs, drivers, vehicles, supplier_offerings, allowed_driver_ids=None, allowed_supplier_ids=None, allow_override_days=None, travel_buffer_minutes=DEFAULT_TRAVEL_BUFFER_MINUTES)  # 0 as of 2026-08-03, was 30 -- see TB-001
key_functions.algorithm_summary: For each job in time order: try in-house (qualifying + not off + shift period matches + no overlap + no daily/monthly overtime violation, pick a candidate, then find any free matching vehicle -- or, for a 'Driver Only' row, no vehicle at all, see _vehicle_type_needs_vehicle). Candidate ranking (2026-08-03, NEW-007): for a 'Same Driver' group (see below) it's plain least-occupied-hours; for an UNGROUPED job it's specialist-reservation first -- min(candidates, key=lambda d: (-len(d.license_types), d.occupied_seconds)) -- preferring the more broadly-licensed ('generalist') candidate over a narrowly-licensed ('specialist') one, so a driver who is the ONLY qualifier for some vehicle type has their hours reserved for that exclusive work rather than spent on a job a generalist could equally cover. Can't push anyone over their own ceiling since the hard-rule filter already excludes any candidate who'd violate it before this ranking runs. Deliberately NOT applied to grouped jobs (including a group's first-ever assignment) -- tried it, and since neither driver is in group_drivers[group_key] yet for an opening row, it stole the row away from a specialist toward a generalist, fragmenting a block that should stay on one driver; group continuity already handles consolidation correctly on its own. If no in-house driver+vehicle combo found, try supplier: prefer reusing an already-hired unit from today (any matching offering) that's free; if none, hire a new unit from the offering with lowest cumulative_hours_history among those with remaining daily capacity, naming it via SupplierHire.label convention. 'Same Driver' groups (job.same_driver_key): tracks group_drivers/group_vehicle_by_driver/group_supplier_hires registries; prefers reusing the driver/vehicle/supplier-hire already used for that group before considering others, and relaxes the overlap check between rows sharing the same group_key -- BUT (fixed 2026-08-03, SD-004 in the scheduling rules spec) only when the candidate driver's already-established vehicle for that group is the SAME TYPE as what the current row needs (or they have none established yet); otherwise the overlap check runs normally, since a driver can't be on two different vehicles at once just because both rows share a group tag -- a real bug found via a live test (one driver on a Chiller Truck and a Bus simultaneously). Only brings in an additional driver/unit when none of the group's current one(s) still qualify for the next row. shift_period is enforced via _job_matches_shift_period() in the candidate loop (replaces the old exact-time shift_start check, removed 2026-08-03 -- see HR-002 rework). The working-hours check: a blank max_overtime_hours_per_month is treated as 0 overtime allowed (a hard daily cap via working_hours_per_day), not as 'unlimited'. The daily ceiling is now d.max_working_hours_per_day (falls back to working_hours_per_day if blank) instead of the old fixed MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY module constant, which was removed 2026-08-03. All hour arithmetic uses _merged_hours() (2026-08-03 fix, see above), not a running sum. AFTER this per-job loop finishes: _fill_gaps_with_unresolved_jobs() runs once (OPT-002/003, added 2026-08-03 -- NOTE: only covers a driver with a genuine BOUNDED gap, booking before AND after; a driver with wide-open, non-bracketed spare capacity is NOT covered -- see NEW-007, partially resolved by the specialist-reservation fix above but the bounded-gap-only limitation itself is unchanged), THEN _repair_minimum_daily_hours() runs looped up to 5x (HR-005, 2026-08-03) -- see each function's own entry below. A real interaction was found 2026-08-03 (Phase 14): giving a generalist a single small ungrouped job via the new specialist-reservation ranking, with nothing else to fill their day, can trip HR-005's under-minimum check and get released to unresolved if no one else has room -- turning an assignable-but-short day into unresolved. Not fixed, tied to the open OPT-001 duty-span/unresolved-policy question. Deliberately NOT done inside this per-job loop itself: a gap-fill preference was tried directly in candidate selection here first and reverted, since jobs are processed in strict start-time order so the LATER of a gap's two bounding jobs is never assigned yet when an earlier job that would sit in that gap is being considered -- it's structurally impossible for an in-loop check to see that gap.
key_functions.note_on_unused_params: allowed_driver_ids and allowed_supplier_ids support a 'restrict to shortlist' feature that has NO UI control yet -- backend-ready, frontend not built

key_functions.name: _driver_has_bounded_gap_fit
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, OPT-002 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: True if job_start/job_end sits strictly BETWEEN one of driver.busy_intervals ending before it and another starting after it (both with the travel buffer) -- i.e. a genuine gap-fill, not merely extending the driver's day earlier or later. Used by _fill_gaps_with_unresolved_jobs() below.

key_functions.name: _fill_gaps_with_unresolved_jobs
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, OPT-002/OPT-003 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: Post-pass, runs once (not looped) right after the main per-job loop, BEFORE _repair_minimum_daily_hours. Confirmed real-world trigger reported by the project owner: a driver got jobs at 13:00-15:00 and 22:00-01:00 (5h work, 7h idle across the 12h span) while a 16:00-20:00 job that fit the gap was left unresolved. For every still-fully-unresolved job (no driver AND no supplier), checks every driver for a bounded gap fit (via _driver_has_bounded_gap_fit) that respects every other hard rule (license/off-day/shift/overlap/ceiling/monthly-cap), and assigns it there instead of leaving it unresolved. Does NOT reclaim a job already given to a supplier -- unwinding a SupplierHire safely is separate, riskier work not attempted. Skips 'Same Driver' grouped jobs.
key_functions.returns: bool -- True if anything was filled (currently unused by the caller, kept for symmetry with _repair_minimum_daily_hours's return value and potential future looping)

key_functions.name: _repair_minimum_daily_hours
key_functions.added: 2026-08-03, HR-005 in the scheduling rules spec
key_functions.purpose: Post-pass hard rule: a driver used at all on a day must reach working_hours_per_day that day. For every (day, driver) left under-minimum, tries to move ALL of that driver's jobs that day to another qualifying driver with room (same license/off-day/shift/overlap/ceiling/monthly-cap checks as the main loop); if every job can move, commits the move, else releases the whole day to unresolved with an explicit note. Skips jobs inside a 'Same Driver' group. Does not attempt a supplier fallback for a released day (flagged for manual review instead). Best-effort greedy heuristic, not a global optimizer -- see CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 10 for the disclosed limitation and NEXT_SESSION.md for the still-open real-data validation.
key_functions.bug_fixed_2026_08_03: Phase 11: originally snapshotted every (day, driver)'s job list ONCE at the start and iterated the static snapshot -- a fix for one driver could leave a LATER driver's entry in the same pass reasoning about stale data, causing jobs to visibly ping-pong between two drivers instead of settling (caught by tests/test_gap_filling.py). Fixed by recomputing each pair's actual current jobs/total fresh from `jobs` immediately before processing it. A second latent bug (multiple jobs moved to the same replacement driver in one batch weren't checked against each other's tentative hours/overlap, so two individually-legal moves could jointly exceed a hard rule) was fixed at the same time by tracking tentative per-driver/per-vehicle additions within a batch before anything is committed.
key_functions.returns: bool -- True if anything changed, used by allocate()'s calling loop to decide whether another pass might help

modules.fairness_model: hours-occupied, not job-count. min(candidates, key=lambda d: d.occupied_seconds)

supplier_naming_convention.priority: always try to reuse an already-hired unit before hiring a new one, to minimize headcount for the day
supplier_naming_convention.note: user's own historical manually-planned reference files are inconsistent about this numbering (some suppliers numbered, some not) -- confirmed by user this is a manual-entry artifact, NOT the desired behavior; the engine's consistent numbering is correct and should not be changed to match old files

overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_null_or_bla: no overtime allowed at all -- working_hours_per_day becomes a strict daily ceiling (fixed to fail-closed some time ago; this entry was previously stale/wrong here, saying 'unlimited' -- corrected 2026-08-03)
overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_zero: same as blank -- no overtime allowed at all
overtime_model.max_overtime_hours_per_month_positive: monthly overtime budget, checked against finalized_jobs history
overtime_model.daily_ceiling: max_working_hours_per_day (per-driver, planner-set, e.g. 12 paired with working_hours_per_day=9). Null/blank falls back to working_hours_per_day (zero daily overtime). Replaces the old fixed MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY module constant, removed 2026-08-03 -- see HR-002 rework.
overtime_model.daily_minimum: NEW 2026-08-03 (HR-005). A driver used at all on a day must reach at least working_hours_per_day that day. Enforced as a post-pass repair (_repair_minimum_daily_hours), not a per-job filter -- see that function's entry above.

confirmed_with_owner: Overlapping times within a flagged group are allowed for the same driver (not a conflict).
No hard-coded time-based or vehicle-type-based split -- fewest additional drivers/units possible, via reuse-first preference.
same_driver_group_feature.known_simplification: occupied_seconds and monthly overtime projection still SUM every row's duration even when same-group rows overlap, rather than computing a true elapsed-time union. Overstates rather than understates hours -- intentional, given Rule 6 (driver safety is a hard constraint).
tested_with: real UNPLANNED.xlsx + fleetplanner.db (all 9 real flagged groups resolved correctly)
test_same_driver.py (synthetic: forced split, overlap relaxation, regression check)

important_constants_in_this_module.MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY: REMOVED 2026-08-03. Was 2.0, a hard per-day overtime ceiling on top of working_hours_per_day, global/not per-driver configurable. Replaced by the per-driver DriverProfile.max_working_hours_per_day field -- see HR-002 rework, CHANGELOG_AI.md Phase 10.
important_constants_in_this_module.SHIFT_PERIOD_EVENING_CUTOFF_HOUR: NEW 2026-08-03. Currently 12 (noon) -- the hour-of-day boundary _job_matches_shift_period() uses to decide morning vs evening. A single global constant, not per-driver configurable, since the planner only asked for a simple morning/evening split.

modules.responsibility: One job: HTTP call to Google Routes API, parse response, raise MapsClientError on failure. Knows nothing about jobs/drivers/allocation.

key_functions.name: get_travel_time
key_functions.raises: MapsClientError on any failure (missing key, bad response, no route found)
key_functions.important_detail: uses routingPreference=TRAFFIC_AWARE and passes the job's ACTUAL departure time (converted to RFC3339 UTC via _to_rfc3339) -- this is why the same route can return different estimates depending on time of day, which was an explicit requirement

modules.responsibility: Builds AI context payload, calls Claude, parses JSON response into suggestions. Never mutates a Job directly -- only returns suggestion dicts.

key_functions.name: build_review_context
key_functions.signature: build_review_context(jobs, event_groups, driver_hours_summary, travel_time_lookups, day_notes, preferences_digest='')
key_functions.returns: dict with keys: events_with_multiple_stages, driver_occupied_hours_today, travel_time_lookups_minutes, planner_day_notes, planner_preferences_digest
key_functions.note: filters event_groups to only events with >=2 stages -- single-stage events have nothing to reason about

key_functions.name: review_plan
key_functions.returns: list[suggestion dict] with keys: type, affected_jobs, reasoning
key_functions.note: defensively strips markdown code fences from the response before JSON parsing, since the model sometimes wraps output despite instructions not to

system_prompt_responsibilities: reason about event-chain stay-on-site vs cycle-back decisions using travel time + gap + driver remaining hours
weigh travel-time confidence (exact vs approximate, from Locations tab resolution) -- more conservative suggestions on approximate data
read planner day-notes and propose specific overrides only when clearly supported
flag conflicts revealed by real travel times
use planner_preferences_digest as guidance, not a hard rule
NEVER change the plan itself -- suggestions only
respond ONLY with valid JSON matching the fixed suggestion schema

modules.responsibility: Compresses decision_log into the small preference_digest. Planner-triggered only (Settings tab button), never automatic -- deliberate cost control.

key_functions.name: refresh_digest
key_functions.behavior: reads db.get_decisions_since(conn, existing_digest.covered_through_date); if empty, returns existing digest UNCHANGED and makes ZERO API calls (verified by test, not just intent); otherwise sends existing digest + only the new decisions to Claude, saves the merged result with an updated covered_through_date watermark
key_functions.cost_guarantee: old decisions are never resent on subsequent refreshes -- confirmed via test with decisions across multiple dates and two refresh calls

modules.responsibility: Loads the ORIGINAL uploaded workbook, writes only Vehicle/Driver columns for matched rows, saves as a new file. Regenerates nothing.

key_functions.name: export_filled_excel
key_functions.raises: ValueError if Vehicle/Driver columns aren't found in the header row
key_functions.behavior: openpyxl.load_workbook(original_path) preserves all styles/formatting; finds Vehicle/Driver column indices by header text; for each job matched by row_number, writes driver_text (driver name, or supplier label if supplier-assigned) and vehicle_text (plate, or blank for supplier jobs) into ONLY those two cells; unresolved jobs get both left blank
key_functions.verified: tested against a real file -- confirmed row/column counts unchanged, header font/formatting unchanged, an untouched column (Event) byte-identical before/after

database_schema.migration_system: additive only (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, swallows duplicate-column errors); new tables via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; does NOT support column rename/retype/removal

columns.name: active
columns.note: NOT actually used for filtering -- delete_driver does a hard DELETE

columns.name: working_hours_per_day
columns.business_rule: baseline/normal daily hours. Also the hard daily MINIMUM as of 2026-08-03 (HR-005): a driver used at all on a day must reach at least this many hours that day, enforced via a post-pass repair (see allocation_engine._repair_minimum_daily_hours).

columns.name: shift_start
columns.business_rule: DEPRECATED 2026-08-03, replaced by shift_period below. No longer read by allocation_engine.py; column kept only so old data isn't lost.

columns.name: shift_period
columns.business_rule: 'morning' | 'evening' | NULL (no restriction). Replaces shift_start's exact-time model -- the planner sets a simple label, not a clock time; the engine enforces a window (morning=before 12:00, evening=12:00 onward). No automatic rotation logic -- explicitly rejected, see spec SS-002.

columns.name: max_overtime_hours_per_month

business_rules: In-house drivers/vehicles are always attempted before any supplier for every job, independently, in time order -- no pre-reservation of jobs for suppliers.
Fairness among in-house drivers is measured by cumulative occupied HOURS, not job count.
A driver's license_types must contain an EXACT (case/whitespace-normalized) match for a job's vehicle_type_required, or the driver is not considered at all for that job.

A job's time-of-day must match a driver's shift_period ('morning'=before 12:00, 'evening'=12:00 onward, None=no restriction). Replaces the old exact-time shift_start model 2026-08-03 -- the planner no longer fixes an exact clock time before planning, just a Morning/Evening label; no automatic rotation. See HR-002 rework.
Off days are a hard skip unless explicitly overridden for a specific date (allow_override_days parameter, no UI yet).
max_overtime_hours_per_month: NULL/blank = no overtime allowed at all (same as 0); positive number = monthly budget checked against finalized_jobs history.
Supplier hiring always tries to REUSE an already-hired unit before hiring a new one, to minimize the day's headcount, even if it means one supplier driver works more hours.
New supplier hires are chosen from the offering with the LOWEST cumulative historical hours among suppliers with remaining daily capacity, for cross-day fairness.

Supplier unit naming: 1st hire = bare supplier name, 2nd hire = 'NAME 1', Nth = 'NAME {N-1}', reuse = 'SAME <label>'. This is user-confirmed and should not be changed based on old inconsistent manual reference files.
A vehicle is unavailable if EITHER in_workshop OR excluded_from_planning is set -- they are treated as equivalent for allocation purposes.
AI suggestions never change the plan automatically -- every suggestion requires an explicit planner Accept/Reject click.

The raw decision_log is never sent to Claude -- only the small, periodically-refreshed preference_digest is included in daily AI Review calls, to keep cost/latency flat over time regardless of history length.
Export must preserve the original uploaded file exactly, changing only the Vehicle and Driver cell values for matched rows -- no reformatting, no regeneration from a template.
Unresolved jobs (no valid assignment found) are never written to finalized_jobs.
Events (grouped by event_id) with 2+ stages are the unit of reasoning for the AI's stay-on-site-vs-cycle-back judgment; single-stage events are excluded from that reasoning entirely.

The 'Same Driver' Excel column lets the planner flag rows that should be handled by one driver back-and-forth; overlapping times within such a flagged group are allowed for the same driver, and the engine brings in the fewest additional drivers/supplier units possible rather than a hard-coded time or vehicle-type split.
A blank 'Max overtime/month' for a driver is treated the same as an explicit 0 (no overtime allowed) -- working_hours_per_day still applies as a hard daily cap in that case.

License-type qualification (a driver must hold the exact vehicle type license for a job) was audited at the project owner's request in an earlier session and confirmed correctly enforced -- no bug found here.

A driver's daily ceiling is max_working_hours_per_day (planner-set per driver, e.g. 12), on top of working_hours_per_day, regardless of remaining monthly overtime budget. Replaces the old fixed, global MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY=2.0 constant 2026-08-03 -- see HR-002 rework. Blank falls back to working_hours_per_day (zero daily overtime).

NEW 2026-08-03 (HR-005): a driver used at all on a day must reach at least working_hours_per_day that day (hard minimum, not just a target). Enforced as a post-allocation repair pass, not a per-job filter, since the engine can't know a day's total until its last job is considered -- see allocation_engine._repair_minimum_daily_hours.

workflows.name: daily_planning_workflow
steps: 1. Upload Excel file -> excel_import.load_jobs_from_excel -> list[Job] in memory
3. Run Planning -> allocation_engine.allocate() mutates jobs -> results table rendered, filter dropdown populated
4. (optional) AI Review -> travel-time lookups via maps_client + db.resolve_location -> ai_review.review_plan() -> suggestion cards with Accept/Reject
5. (per suggestion) Accept/Reject -> db.log_decision (does NOT auto-update the table -- known gap)
6. Finalize Day -> db.save_finalized_jobs (skips unresolved jobs, overwrites existing rows for that date)
7. Export Filled Excel -> export.export_filled_excel writes into a COPY of the original file, saved wherever the planner chooses

workflows.name: digest_refresh_workflow
workflows.trigger: manual, planner clicks 'Refresh Preferences Digest Now' in Settings tab
steps: 1. db.get_digest -> existing digest text + covered_through_date watermark
3. If none new: return existing digest unchanged, ZERO API calls made
4. If new decisions exist: send existing digest + new decisions to Claude, get merged/updated digest text (capped ~400 words)
5. db.save_digest with new watermark = latest decision's plan_date

workflows.name: master_data_setup_workflow
workflows.description: one-time-ish setup, edited only when something changes (new driver, rate change, vehicle to workshop)

architectural_decisions.decision: Standalone single-user desktop app, not multi-user web app
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Only one planner uses the actual software; supervisor/drivers only ever see the exported file distributed externally. Eliminated need for hosting/accounts/real-time sync entirely.

architectural_decisions.decision: Deterministic engine and AI review are two separate, manually-triggered steps, not automatically combined
architectural_decisions.reasoning: While the deterministic engine was (and still is, to some degree) being actively debugged, keeping AI out of the automatic loop made every discovered issue traceable to one layer or the other. A combined one-click shortcut is a deliberately deferred future addition.

architectural_decisions.decision: AI never finalizes anything automatically -- suggestions require explicit Accept/Reject
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Non-negotiable requirement from the first design discussion; human stays in control of every change.

architectural_decisions.decision: Two-tier decision history: full local log (never sent) + small periodically-refreshed digest (only thing sent)
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Answers 'does the AI learn over time' honestly (the model is stateless per call) while letting the SYSTEM reflect accumulated real decisions without unbounded cost/latency growth.

architectural_decisions.decision: Hard rules moved from free-text rule-line parsing to structured database columns
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Directly caused by two real bugs (a driver's hour cap silently unenforced due to un-matched phrasing; later, shift_start type of issue) where free-text matching failed silently. Structured fields with explicit format-hint UI eliminate the ambiguity.

architectural_decisions.decision: Supplier units are generated dynamically at planning time, never pre-named by the planner
architectural_decisions.reasoning: The original 'pre-name your trucks' model was identified as backwards -- the app should decide unit numbering based on actual daily demand, not have the planner guess in advance.

architectural_decisions.decision: Export loads and modifies the ORIGINAL workbook rather than regenerating from a template
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Explicit requirement: output must be byte-identical to the input except for the Vehicle/Driver cells -- no reformatting risk.

architectural_decisions.decision: Settings PIN disables the tab entirely rather than switch-then-revert
architectural_decisions.reasoning: The switch-then-revert approach could flash tab contents before the check completed -- a real, observed issue, fixed by disabling the tab outright while locked.

architectural_decisions.decision: Additive-only schema migrations (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN)
architectural_decisions.reasoning: After multiple rounds of asking the user to delete their local database for schema changes, this was added so small future field additions don't cause data loss. Structural changes (rename/retype/remove) still require a fresh database.

architectural_decisions.decision: Vehicle-type matching is exact string comparison, never fuzzy
architectural_decisions.reasoning: Deliberately rejected fuzzy matching as riskier than the problem it solves (risk of silently conflating genuinely different vehicle configurations). Real-world text mismatches are treated as a data-entry/process problem to fix at the source, not a matching-algorithm problem to work around.

important_constants.name: DEFAULT_TRAVEL_BUFFER_MINUTES
important_constants.changed_2026_08_03: was 30. Confirmed with the project owner (TB-001 in the scheduling rules spec): a planner-set end time already accounts for travel back to base -- e.g. 05:00-08:00 followed by 08:00-11:00 for the same driver is intentional, 08:00 IS the chosen return-to-base time, not a shorthand needing a buffer added on top. A non-zero buffer was double-counting travel time already built into the planner's chosen times and blocking real back-to-back continuations between unrelated orders. Re-running a full real-file reconstruction after this change took it from 42/44 to 44/44 rows auto-assigned. FUTURE WORK: once live Google Maps travel-time lookups are wired in, gaps between jobs at genuinely different locations should be checked against real drive time instead of trusting manual timing -- a distance-aware replacement for this flat constant, not a reason to raise it back to a flat non-zero value in the meantime.
important_constants.purpose: minimum gap enforced between two jobs assigned to the same driver or vehicle; 0 means adjacent/zero-gap jobs are allowed, only genuine time overlap is a conflict

important_constants.name: MAX_DIGEST_WORDS
important_constants.purpose: caps preference_digest size regardless of how much history feeds into it

important_constants.name: SHIFT_PERIOD_EVENING_CUTOFF_HOUR
important_constants.purpose: hour-of-day boundary for morning vs evening shift_period. Replaces MAX_OVERTIME_HOURS_PER_DAY (removed 2026-08-03) at this spot in the constants list -- the daily overtime ceiling is now the per-driver max_working_hours_per_day field, not a module constant. See HR-002 rework.

real_world_validation_performed.method: user pushed a real fleetplanner.db snapshot plus a real day's UNPLANNED.xlsx/PLANNED.xlsx pair to a public GitHub repo specifically for AI testing
findings_were_mostly_data_issues_not_cod: All 11 drivers in the snapshot had identical license_types ('5 Ton Chiller Truck (with lift)'), blocking 95 of 125 real jobs from ever going in-house
Only 4 in-house chiller trucks existed in the snapshot, 2 legitimately locked for a full 12-hour event
A driver (VENUGOPAL) present in the planned reference was missing from the database entirely
A vehicle-type text mismatch ('23 Seater Bus' entered vs '23 Seated Bus' required) caused a silent zero-match
real_world_validation_performed.code_bug_found_via_this_process: shift_start field missing from DriverProfile dataclass -- see allocation_engine module entry above
real_world_validation_performed.tooling_built_during_validation: a one-off script extracting suggested license_types per driver directly from PLANNED.xlsx by grouping historical Driver->VehicleType pairs; applied to a test database copy, improved match rate from 4% to 7% (confirming license types were a real factor but not the sole explanation)
